correctness.rationale: There are eight free binary coordinates and all 65,536 ordered pairs are in scope. Monotone bracket closure of a linear span computes ordinary Lie generation: each insertion lies in any candidate generated subalgebra and bilinearity gives closure once its basis brackets are included. For the second method the normalizer of a linear space is a Lie algebra by Jacobi; stability under ad(A) and ad(B) therefore suffices when the space lies in the generated algebra and contains A and B. Independent exhaustive code, not the frozen verifier, recovered counts (1,765,3618,7392,20160,20160,0,0,13440), probability 105/512, and directly partitioned the generating pairs into 80 orbits of size 168. A simultaneous stabilizer commutes with the six off-diagonal matrix units and is scalar, hence trivial in GL3(F2); the group order is (8−1)(8−2)(8−4). The coordinate-line stabilizer really has 64 elements and is Lie closed; every pair in it has rank at most five in the generation census. The zero bins concern pair-generated dimensions only. Direct replay: python3 /workspace/branches/651578e9-bee0-45f5-873e-3b4a0ba1a5b7/independent_census.py; exact output independent_census.out in the same directory. This is an exhaustive finite computation, not a formal machine proof or a result at other fields/ranks.
